sessions.title: Introduction to Lacanian Psychoanalysis
sessions.description:

-Imaginary, Symbolic, Real
-Phallus
-Signifier, Signified

-Unconscious
-Big Other
-Desire
-Jouissance
-Fantasy

materials.note: Lacan, J. (2006). In B. Fink (Trans.), Écrits. (pp 75-81). New York & London: W.W Norton.

materials.title: The mirror stage (Commentary on Lacan’s ‘The mirror-stage’)
The function and field of speech and language in psychoanalysis
materials.note: Lacan, J. (2006). In B. Fink (Trans.), Écrits. (pp. 197-268). New York & London: W.W Norton.

materials.title: Six Moments in Lacan
On dreams
The Lacanian Subject
materials.note: Fink, B. (1995). Princeton University Press. (Chapter 4: The Lacanian Subject).

materials.title: Lacan to the letter
materials.note: Fink, B. (2004). Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press. (Chapter 3: Reading “The instance of the letter in the unconscious”).

materials.title: Against Understanding: Commentary and Critique in a Lacanian Key, Volume 1
materials.note: Fink, B. (2014). London & New York. Routledge. (Chapter 1).

materials.title: How are we to understand the body, and embodiment, via the notion of the mirror stage?
What is included within the remit of the imaginary?
How can we differentiate between the imaginary and the symbolic registers?
What is ‘the Other’, and how does this concept inform clinical work and forms of ideology critique?
What crucial concepts from Freud’s analysis of dreams are foundational to the Lacanian credo that the unconscious is structured like a language?
Why does the notion of the signifier feature so prominently in Lacan’s understanding of the unconscious?
How should one understand Lacan’s idea that the unconscious can be understood as ‘the discourse of the Other’?
How, following Lacan, are jouissance and desire to be differentiated?
What is the relation of the phallus to language?
Why is there a different relation to the phallus as signifier for those designated as ‘men’ opposed to those designated as ‘women’?
The Pervert’s Guide to Cinema (2006)
Lacan and contemporary film
materials.note: McGowan, T., & Kunkle, S. (Eds.). (2004). Other Press (Introduction: Lacanian Psychoanalysis in Film Theory).

materials.title: How has Lacanian film theory changed in recent years?
With which register(s) (Imaginary, Symbolic, and/or Real) does contemporary Lacanian film theory concern itself? In what way?
What was/is the role of ideology in cinema and its critique?
What is the role of the spectator?

data.notes: Class will meet once a week, but I would also like to host weekly movie nights at CILAS that are open to the public. Discussions/readings of the films will take place in class. I have included a list of proposed films, but all of these are subject to change with participant feedback; I prefer that we make our selections as a group.
